messages:
Matt: Heads-up: I'm drafting the prefix-cache API contract for streaming responses. Quick decision needed: do we guarantee the cache hit indicator on partial streaming chunks or only emit it on the final chunk? Need this for SDK fallback logic and for Dedicated routing. cc @Jenny @Sam

Jenny: My vote: only set the hit boolean on the final chunk/event. If we set it mid-stream clients will need to react mid-response which is a pain. Keep x-rw-cache-hit as terminal.

Sam: Agree leaning final-only. Curious if we should offer a tri-state or status field though, so SDKs can show "partial" vs full hit. e.g., x-rw-cache-status: miss|partial|hit

Kris: I'd avoid a boolean+string duplication. Proposal: keep a boolean x-rw-cache-hit for backward compatibility (final-only), and add x-rw-cache-status on the final response with {miss,partial,hit}. Old clients will keep reading the boolean and ignore status. New clients can prefer status.

Matt: That sounds reasonable. Also want to consider streaming interim metadata — do we send progress or any header pre-final? I'm wary of adding more streaming headers unless we have a concrete use case.

Jenny: If we must expose partial info, I'd prefer a single final header shape. Interim headers = more complexity.

Sam: If we add x-rw-cache-status, can we avoid changing existing SDK parsing? Node/Go client currently looks for x-cache-hit exact header. We need a migration plan.

deploy-bot: prefix-cache-rfc v2 pushed: https://git.internal/rw/infra/rfcs/122 -- CI: green :white_check_mark:

Kris: Edge-case: invalidation while streaming. If an upstream invalidate arrives mid-stream, do we mark the final response stale? We should include a mechanism to indicate validation time or TTL used. Maybe x-rw-cache-validated-at or x-rw-cache-ttl-seconds.

Jenny: Also for debugging it'd be useful to include a cache-key fingerprint, BUT we must avoid PII. So include hashed key: x-rw-cache-key: sha256:<hex> and document that it's salted per-customer. Add KMS note in RFC.

Matt: Action items: (1) Jenny to draft explicit header semantics + backward compat note in RFC, (2) Sam to audit SDKs for header parsing & fallback, (3) Kris to write invalidation story + TTL/validated-at examples. I'll file the release note checklist for SDKs. Target: EOD Thu. @Sam can you ack?

Sam: Ack. I'll add test matrix for Node/Go/Python and validate both boolean and status parsing. Quick Q: keep boolean header name 'x-rw-cache-hit' or 'x-cache-hit'? I prefer namespacing to avoid collisions.

Jenny: Agree use namespaced short form: 'x-rw-cache-hit' + 'x-rw-cache-status' + 'x-rw-cache-key'. That keeps it compact and unique.

Matt: OK using x-rw-* headers. Example (final response):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rw-cache-status: partial
x-rw-cache-hit: false
x-rw-cache-key: sha256:3f2a1b...
x-rw-cache-ttl-seconds: 34
Content-Type: application/json

{ ... streaming body ended ... }
```

Matt: Notes: x-rw-cache-hit only present on final response; x-rw-cache-status present on final; x-rw-cache-key is hashed+salted; x-rw-cache-ttl-seconds optional for debugging. We'll avoid interim progress headers for now.

Jenny: I'll open the doc PR with those exact header names and compatibility section.

Sam: I'll add parsing tests and fallback (treat missing x-rw-cache-status as unknown).

Kris: I'll draft the invalidation scenario and what we surface when invalidate occurs mid-response (recommendation: mark response as stale in status and include x-rw-cache-invalidated-at timestamp).

Jenny: PR: https://git.internal/rw/infer/pull/420 — includes header schema + examples. Please review. :thumbsup:
